summary: party-search escapes LIKE wildcards (% and _) and the escape char in user input so the name filter matches a literal substring.
reason: soqlQuote only doubles single quotes; it left % and _ as active SoQL LIKE wildcards (e.g. 'MADISON_AVE' matched 'MADISON AVE'). Added soqlLikePattern/soqlLikeEscaper to backslash-escape %, _ and \. Socrata SoQL uses backslash as LIKE's default escape char and REJECTS an explicit `ESCAPE` clause (HTTP 400), so the clause is omitted — verified live against the real Parties dataset.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli (TestSoqlLikePattern) plus live party-search: 'MADISON' returns matches, 'MADISON_AVE' returns 0 (literal underscore), '50%' returns results with no SoQL error.
